claims.text: Replacing elemental Cr with an AlNbTiZr MEA coating will suppress elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The AlNbTiZr coating will prevent premature coating failure.
The AlNbTiZr coating will provide robust corrosion protection under normal PWR water conditions.
The AlNbTiZr coating will provide oxidation protection in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
AlNbTiZr MEA coatings can be deposited on zirconium-alloy substrates by RF magnetron co-sputtering.
Typical PWR primary-water operation occurs at approximately 300–350°C.
AlNbTiZr coatings have a composite amorphous and bcc-nanocrystalline microstructure.
The composite coating microstructure creates a dense oxide layer.
The AlNbTiZr coating forms a diffusion barrier at the coating–substrate interface.
Al and Nb promote formation of a dense, corrosion-resistant oxide layer.
Including Zr in the coating enhances metallurgical bonding to the Zr-alloy substrate.
Lattice distortion in the multielement coating raises the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
The raised diffusion activation energy reduces Cr and Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperature.
Pure Cr coatings undergo elevated-temperature interdiffusion with zirconium substrates, leading to cracking or peeling under LOCA conditions.
Relative to a pure-Cr-coated baseline, the AlNbTiZr coating will have a significantly thinner interdiffusion zone.
Relative to a pure-Cr-coated baseline, the AlNbTiZr coating will have enhanced oxidation resistance.
Relative to a pure-Cr-coated baseline, the AlNbTiZr coating will retain better mechanical integrity after PWR-water and high-temperature-steam exposure.

contradictions.description: The intervention completely replaces elemental Cr with an AlNbTiZr coating, yet the proposed mechanism, predicted outcome, and falsification rule continue to treat Cr–Zr interdiffusion as the relevant interfacial process in the modified specimen. Unless residual Cr is explicitly retained, there is no Cr in the proposed coating whose interdiffusion zone can be measured.
